supports: Exact source representatives; Falkland shelf to 300 m; exclusion of adult toothfish, certain deeper skates and grenadiers; no quantitative small/large demersal cutoffs. Table 2 is 35 groups, but native and Table 4 separate Discards and Detritus to give 36 source groups.

title: Souto and Giberto (2026), benthic habitat research plan for Pleoticus muelleri fishery
supports: INIDEP describes benthic-demersal life habit and exploited concentrations at 41-47 degrees S. Retrieved search abstract; page open returned no text.

title: WoRMS Pleoticus muelleri accepted taxon
supports: Accepted marine shrimp; decapod connection. Search entry available; direct page returned 403.

title: WoRMS Munida taxon list
supports: Source Munida gregaria is currently accepted as Grimothea gregaria. Preserve native source spelling; this does not turn shrimps into explicit members.

title: Alemany et al. (2021), coastal assemblage El Rincon 39-41.5 degrees S
supports: Study of 591 hauls in 1994-2012; Table 2 calls Micropogonias furnieri and Cynoscion guatucupa bony demersal fishes. Journal table search extract inspected; direct PDF open timed out.

title: Denadai et al. (2015), feeding habits of Micropogonias furnieri
supports: Primary trawl study in Caraguatatuba Bay: primarily small immature fish; diet includes crustaceans, bivalve siphons and polychaetes; benthic carnivory. Feeding is supplementary evidence, not a matching gate or adult-catch composition estimate.

title: Laptikhovsky, Arkhipkin and Brickle, Biology and Distribution of Grenadiers around Falkland Islands
supports: Macrourus carinatus caught at 173-1201 m, most abundant 700-1000 m; M. holotrachys mostly >900 m; source Coelorinchus fasciatus is a smaller macrourid, occurring 114-982 m and mainly 200-600 m. Search publisher abstract inspected; direct page returned 403.

title: Eschmeyer Catalog of Fishes, Genypterus brasiliensis (updated 13 August 2026)
supports: Currently valid separate species despite historical synonymy with G. blacodes. SW Atlantic range Brazil south to Bahia San Matias, Argentina. Genus catch is not automatically exact G. blacodes.

title: Argentine fisheries filet identification catalog
supports: Recognizes G. blacodes and G. brasiliensis as two national species; supports real genus composition uncertainty.

title: CCAMLR Species Description 2021: Dissostichus eleginoides
supports: Juveniles under 50 cm use continental shelf; larger maturity-stage fish move deeper than 500 m. Supports real stage/depth mismatch with juvenile-only focal source.

title: Morphological and Molecular Evidence Reveals Zearaja brevicaudata as Senior Synonym of Dipturus lamillai
supports: Primary morphology/genetics paper supports synonymy of source Dipturus lamillai with Zearaja brevicaudata and distinctness from Chilean Z. chilensis. Do not infer Z. chilensis catch label is the source exact taxon without checking usage.

title: Argentine National Parks SIB Bathyraja albomaculata
supports: Source Bathyraja belongs to Arhynchobatidae under current classification, not Rajidae. Historical Rajidae reporting can be broader; common catch name Stingrays conflicts with current family name.

title: Eschmeyer Catalog of Fishes Cynoscion species list
supports: Current C. striatus is a synonym of C. guatucupa (nomen oblitum); preserve both catch labels separately. Search full entry inspected; direct page returned 403.

title: FAO 2014 Yearbook aquaculture species categories
supports: FAO reports Finfishes nei and Marine fishes nei as Osteichthyes in this reporting context. This supports a possible bony-fish category restriction, but is not a verified crosswalk to the focal SAU catch labels. General finfish usage alone is insufficient to decide eligibility.
